# Bifrost

> Bifrost is a Go library for server-side rendering React components with QuickJS. It bridges Go backends with React frontends, rendering in-process with no external JS runtime.

Bifrost enables Go HTTP servers to render React components on the server with a small API. React SSR uses `renderToString` and streams the response with `103 Early Hints`, flushing the static head before the props loader and render. Static pages are pre-rendered at build time into HTML with client-side React hydration (MPA-style). Development hot reload is handled by `bifrost dev` with built-in reverse proxy. Production deployment uses embedded assets for single binary distribution.

## Features

- Server-side rendering of React components
- Props loading from Go to React
- MPA-style static pages with pre-rendered HTML + client hydration
- Hot reload via `bifrost dev` (build+proxy+watcher)
- Single binary deployment with embedded assets
- Strict production builds: any required page or bundle failure exits non-zero
- Content-hashed production assets with immutable browser caching
- Project scaffolding with templates (`minimal`, `spa`)

## Template Options

When creating a new project, choose from:
- `minimal` (default): Basic SSR setup with props loading
- `spa`: Client-only single page application with `WithClient()`

## API

Bifrost v1 supports React only. Build-scanned `Page` declarations use string-literal component paths and direct Bifrost option calls; unsupported indirect forms fail instead of being skipped. `WithLoader` is SSR-only. Client-only pages always use an empty shell and do not server-render `Head`.

```go
app, err := bifrost.New(
    bifrostFS,
    bifrost.Page("/{$}", "./pages/home.tsx", bifrost.WithLoader(loadProps)),
    bifrost.Page("/about", "./pages/about.tsx", bifrost.WithClient()),
    bifrost.Page("/blog", "./pages/blog.tsx", bifrost.WithStatic()),
)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
defer app.Stop()

api := chi.NewRouter()
handler := app.Wrap(api)
// Serve handler with http.Server and graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown so app.Stop runs.
```
